summary: Ayya Khema (1923–1997) was a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under Laurence Khantipalo Mills, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Narada Mahathera, and Matara Sri Nyanarama, and served as a teacher at Buddha-Haus in 1989.

Ayyadurai Dhamotharan is an Indologist and linguist who earned his BA at Annamalai University and his PhD under V. I. Subramoniam at the University of Kerala. He lectured at Annamalai and served as Lecturer of Tamil at Heidelberg University (1969–2000).
Azizah Nur is an academic who, as attested in 2026, pursued PhD studies at the Australian National University under the supervision of Assa Doron.

B. Alan Wallace (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Amherst College and earned his PhD at Stanford under Carl Bielefeldt. He taught at Rabten Choeling, UC Santa Barbara, and headed the Santa Barbara Institute.

B. N. Goswamy (1933–2023) was an art historian and Indologist. He studied at Panjab University (~1950–1961), served in the Indian Administrative Service (~1956–1958), and later held a post at Panjab University (~1965–1993).

B. N. Hebbar is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. As attested in 1999, he served as Adjunct Professor of Eastern Religions at George Washington University and Director of Education at Vishva Madhva Sangha.

B. N. K. Sharma (1909–2005) specialized in Indology and philosophy, earning degrees including a PhD from the University of Madras. He served as principal of Rajah's College, Poornaprajna Sanskrit College, and Dr. A. V. Baliga College, and taught at Ramnarain Ruia College.

B. R. Ambedkar (1891–1956) was a scholar in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from Columbia University and the London School of Economics, and held posts including professor at Sydenham College and principal of Government Law College, Mumbai.

B. R. Gopal (1930–1997) was an Indologist and historian. He held posts as Technical Research Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1964), Epigraphical Assistant for the Government Epigraphist for India (attested 1965), and Epigraphist at Epigraphia Carnatica (attested 1974).

B. R. Sharma is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as Assistant Director of Research at Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005) and as a scientist at the Arid Forest Research Institute in 2020.

Baatr Kitinov is a scholar of history, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology who earned his PhD from Moscow State University. He has served as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Baburam Saksena (1897–1989) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and under Ralph Lilley Turner. He served as Vice-Chancellor of Pt. Ravishankar Shukla University (~1964–1966).

Baden Henry Baden-Powell (1841–1901) was an Indology and history scholar who earned an MA at Oxford. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1861–1889) and as Vice-Chancellor of the University of the Punjab, which he founded.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra (born 1908) studied at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University under Jean Philippe Vogel. An Indologist and archaeologist, he served as Government Epigraphist for India and Assistant and Joint Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India.
Baiei Henmi (1891–1977) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1914–1917) and held a post at Tama Art University (~1953–1968).

Baihui Wu (1919–2014) worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University, served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University, and was a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences.

Baij Nath Puri (1916–1996) was an Indologist and historian who earned his M.Litt. and D.Phil. at Oxford. He served as Professor and Head of Ancient Indian History and Archaeology at the University of Lucknow (~1957–1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak (1856–1920) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Deccan College and Government Law College, Mumbai. He taught at the New English School (~1880–1885) and served as a mathematics teacher at Fergusson College (~1885–1890).

Bal Krishen Thapar (1921–1995) studied at the University of the Punjab, under Mortimer Wheeler, and at Heidelberg University. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981) and Chairman of the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training.
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indology scholar who held posts at Panjab University, where he served as an Assistant (attested 1932) and in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1947).
